metadata.description: Hand-curated high-frequency clinical associations missing from all automated knowledge sources (HPO, OMIM, Orphanet, PrimeKG, docLogica). All values sourced from WHO 2022 classification, NCCN guidelines, and major hematology textbooks.
metadata.rationale: These (finding, disease) pairs are well-established in clinical practice but absent from the structured databases that populate our unified cache. They cover the critical gaps identified in CML vignette coverage analysis.

elevated blast count::chronic myeloid le.note: WHO 2022: CML-BC defined by ≥20% blasts in blood/marrow or extramedullary blast proliferation. Sn~0.95 by definition.

elevated blast count::acute myeloid leuk.note: AML defined by ≥20% myeloid blasts. Sn~0.95 by definition.

elevated blast count::myelodysplastic sy.note: MDS may have elevated blasts (5-19% in MDS-EB); ~40% of MDS have excess blasts. LR near 1 as blasts are common across hematologic malignancies.

anemia::chronic myeloid leukemia, blast.note: CML-BC: anemia present in ~80% due to marrow failure from blast expansion. Low specificity as anemia is ubiquitous.

anemia::acute myeloid leukemia.note: AML: anemia in ~85% at presentation (ineffective erythropoiesis + marrow replacement).

basophilia::myelodysplastic syndrome.note: MDS: basophilia is rare (~5%); its presence argues slightly against MDS vs CML.

leukocytosis::chronic myeloid leukemia,.note: CML-BC often presents with persistent or worsening leukocytosis, though some cases have pancytopenia.

thrombocytopenia::chronic myeloid leukem.note: CML-BC: thrombocytopenia in ~60%, contrasting CML-CP where thrombocytosis is more common.

retinal hemorrhage::chronic myeloid leuk.note: Retinal hemorrhage in CML-BC via leukostasis (WBC >100k). ~15% of hyperleukocytosis cases develop ocular involvement.

retinal hemorrhage::acute myeloid leukem.note: Retinal hemorrhage in AML via leukostasis (especially M4/M5 subtypes). ~20% of cases with hyperleukocytosis.

blurred vision::chronic myeloid leukemia.note: Blurred vision as symptom of leukostasis-related retinopathy. Less specific than retinal hemorrhage.

blurred vision::acute myeloid leukemia.note: Blurred vision as symptom of leukostasis-related retinopathy.

blurred vision::myelodysplastic syndrome.note: Blurred vision rare in MDS; possible via severe anemia but leukostasis unlikely.

splenomegaly::acute myeloid leukemia.note: Splenomegaly in ~30% of AML at presentation. Less prominent than in CML.

leukocytosis::acute myeloid leukemia.note: AML: ~50% present with WBC >10k; ~20% with hyperleukocytosis. WBC can also be low (aleukemic leukemia). LR≈1 as leukocytosis is common across hematologic malignancies.

thrombocytopenia::acute myeloid leukemia.note: AML: thrombocytopenia present in ~75% due to marrow replacement by blasts.

basophilia::acute myeloid leukemia.note: Basophilia rare in AML (~5%); much more characteristic of CML. Mild negative signal for AML.

retinal cotton wool spot::chronic myeloi.note: Cotton-wool spots from leukostasis-related retinal ischemia in CML-BC. ~10% with hyperleukocytosis.

retinal cotton wool spot::acute myeloid.note: Cotton-wool spots from leukostasis-related retinopathy in AML (esp. M4/M5 subtypes).

fatigue::acute myeloid leukemia.note: Fatigue present in ~85% of AML at diagnosis. Extremely low specificity renders LR+≈1.

retinal cotton wool spot::myelodysplasti.note: Cotton-wool spots very rare in MDS; leukostasis unlikely. Possible from severe anemia only.
